summary.intent: Continue orchestrating the GSD `/gsd-plan-phase 70.1` and then `/gsd-execute-phase 70.1` workflows for CipherBox's rotation read-plane durability phase, expanding scope twice per user decisions (Rust engine twin, then desktop FUSE live-wiring), then execute all 13 planned tasks across 7 waves using parallel git worktrees with `pnpm i` per worktree.
summary.outcome: Phase 70.1 was fully planned (13 PLAN.md files, 7 waves, decision-coverage 17/17, plan-checker passed) and executed through Wave 5: Waves 1-4 merged with all post-merge gates green, a genuine product bug in the rotation engine's dirty-frontier ordering (decrypt-before-dirtiness-check) was found by the new depth-3 e2e fixture and fixed in both TS and Rust engines with hardened unit-test mocks, and Wave 5 (FUSE gate-correctness fixes) completed with a documented handoff of 2 failing delete.rs tests to Wave 6/Plan 12.

repo: Decision-coverage gate parser only accepts three D-NN bullet forms (`- **D-NN:** text`, `- **D-NN — title** body`, `- **D-NN: Title.** body`); a bullet like `- **D-NN (title).** body` (period before closing `**`) fails to parse and silently zeroes out coverage for ALL decisions, not just the malformed one
`gsd_run loop render-hooks plan:pre --raw` emits invalid JSON (literal newlines in fragments) — must read the hooks file directly with Read instead of parsing --raw output

`state.planned-phase` and `roadmap.annotate` tools can silently no-op (`updated: []`/`updated: false`) when STATE.md/ROADMAP.md format doesn't match their expected anchors — always verify with a follow-up read, not just trust the tool's echoed success

Worktree executors must scope `cargo fmt`/`clippy` to `-p <crate>` (not workspace-wide) or they strand unrelated formatting drift across dozens of files in the worktree, which blocks `cleanup-wave` merge with `worktree_dirty`

packages/sdk-core's rotation engine unit test mocks made `unsealChildReadKey` unconditionally succeed regardless of key, which masked a real AEAD key-mismatch bug for the entire life of Phase 70 — only a real-crypto e2e fixture with parent-also-rotated dirty edges exposed it

The Rust rotation engine twin (crates/sdk/src/rotation/engine.rs) mirrors TS engine.ts structurally closely enough that bugs found/fixed in one almost always need the identical fix in the other (D-11/D-12/D-13, and the dirty-frontier ordering bug)

`crates/fuse/src/write_ops/rotation_deps.rs` is the new home for the production `RotationDeps` adapter (FuseRotationDeps), sourcing api/owner-keypair/rt from CipherBoxFS (fs.rs:32-37); it was previously stubbed to fail-closed EIO because only a test FakeDeps existed

sdk-e2e (tests/sdk-e2e) has no dotenv loader in its vitest config — running it without first sourcing apps/api/.env causes the harness to fall back to a default TEST_LOGIN_SECRET and 401 with a misleading 'Invalid test login secret' error even when both .env files actually match

apps/web/*.test.ts files are NOT run by CI (web is web-e2e-gated only) — any test logic placed there for browser-only code (e.g. IndexedDB adapters) is effectively uncovered by CI; must be hoisted into packages/sdk with fake-indexeddb to get real CI coverage

rust-analyzer/IDE diagnostics (e.g. a phantom `macros.rs:50` type-mismatch) can be stale/false-positive relative to the authoritative `cargo check`/`cargo test` compile result — trust the compiler over the IDE squiggle

code.finding: collectDirtyFrontier called resolveChildKeyAndEnvelope (which unconditionally AEAD-decrypts the child's sealed ref) before checking childPub.generation > childRef.generation; for a dirty edge whose parent also rotated, decryption throws before the dirtiness check ever runs. Fixed by fetching childPub via resolveAndFetchNode first, comparing generations, and only decrypting confirmed-clean edges (nodeReadKey becomes optional/undefined for dirty items, routed to repairDirtyNode's ECIES checkpoint instead).

resolveChildKeyAndEnvelope bundled 'fetch child's public envelope' and 'decrypt the child's key' into one call with no try/catch, making the ordering bug structurally unavoidable until unsealChildReadKeyFromPub was factored out as a separate step.

DirtyFrontierEntry was the naive 2-field shape (no parent_ipns_name/node_read_key) before Plan 04 widened it; verify_subtree_clean was non-recursive and treated a missing root as clean instead of dirty (fixed at :813-850).

rotate_read_on_scope_exit originally always returned Err(RotationError::RotateFailed) (fail-closed EIO) because the only impl RotationDeps in the workspace was the test FakeDeps — no production adapter existed until Plan 09 built crates/fuse/src/write_ops/rotation_deps.rs.

Test unlink_shared_scope_exit_fails_closed_until_rotation_wired asserted EIO as the expected behavior pre-wiring; it needed to invert once the production adapter was wired (Plan 09/12), and two other private-delete tests started failing after Plan 11's fail-closed gate fix because they seeded a non-authoritative cache (deferred fix to Plan 12).

workflow: Running a single synchronous 'canary' plan first before fanning out N parallel worktree agents is a reasonable risk-mitigation tactic to validate the worktree→commit→SUMMARY→merge mechanic, but must be explicitly communicated to the user as a deliberate choice, not silently done — the user correctly pushed back when it looked like parallelism wasn't happening
When dispatching multiple worktree-isolated agents, fire each Agent call in its own message/turn rather than batching them, because simultaneous `git worktree add` calls race on `.git/config.lock`

After merging a wave that touches multiple packages in a monorepo, rebuild ALL affected dists (not just the one gated in that wave) before running a cross-package consumer's test suite — stale sdk-core dist caused 3 false-positive test failures in the sdk package's post-merge gate
When a coverage/verification tool reports a hard blocking failure, diagnose the actual parser/mechanism (read the source of decisions.cjs) rather than assuming the underlying data is wrong

Delegating root-cause diagnosis to a dedicated debugging subagent with an explicit 'fixture bug vs product bug' framing, and instructing it not to hack the test green, produced a rigorous, evidence-backed verdict (live instrumentation, reverted after) rather than a rushed guess

A tool call that times out (e.g. a slow lint-staged git hook) should be verified via `git log`/`git status` rather than blindly retried — several 'failures' in this session turned out to be false negatives
